name: Kisar
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress; 1 further work by the same author (or citing it for stress) agrees.
catalog_quote: Stress is not phonemic in this language. It occurs on the penultimate syllable of multisyllabic roots. Stress occurs consistently on the penultimate syllable of prefixed and infixed forms. In prefixed monosyllabic roots stress does not occur on the root, rather it occurs on the penultimate syllable of the prefixed form.

audit.reasoning: Identity: the source describes Kisar = Meher = Yotowawa, Austronesian, village of Lebelau on Kisar island (held snippets p. 33) — matches kisa1266, not the Papuan Oirata of the same island. Sourcing: the classification (primary penult; secondary alternating leftward: stress placement coded per word length as 10 010 1010 01010 (1 = a stressed syllable)) rests on the one dedicated phonology of the language, a 1992 SIL chapter with an explicit metrical stress analysis; Glottolog lists nothing newer or better, and the earlier our earlier reading reader reached the same chapter via Google Books and CONFIRMED with no discrepancy.
